input: Kamoi et al. (2024) argue that self-correction papers rarely define their research question: improving on the model's own initial response, improving on the best-possible initial response that uses the same external information, or beating other baseline methods. They find impractical frameworks and unfair evaluations that over-evaluate self-correction. Critique a claim that a gain over the model's own first answer proves that self-correction beats other methods.
source: Kamoi et al. 2024, Abstract and Section 3.1 RQs in Self-Correction Research (chunks kamoi2024-000, kamoi2024-012)
